components.gap: worked boundary not supplied for this exact entry: def:p15-regular-conditional-law (regular-conditional-laws.tex lines 49-51) asserts that the regular-conditional-probability special case (S=Omega, target sigma-algebra F_0, X the identity) needs an existence hypothesis on the outcome space itself, i.e. that without a hypothesis on (Omega,F_0) a regular conditional law need not exist. Nothing on the handbook route demonstrates this: no probability space and sub-sigma-algebra G are exhibited for which no probability kernel from (Omega,G) to (Omega,F_0) satisfies the defining identities, and no argument for the necessity is written. The only support is the citation in conditioning-independence-and-information-w02b-p15-008.tex lines 235-239 to the source, whose p. 214 states nonexistence and attributes it to Dieudonne (1948) without giving the example; that is a citation in place of the owed demonstration. The countable-cocountable model (w02b-p15-008 annex lines 171-269) shows only that a source-sense law can be unrepairable while a regular conditional law exists. Owed: a written model in which no regular conditional probability exists, with its proof, or a written argument establishing the stated need for a hypothesis.

defect_observations.detail: Stale recorded evidence: destination sha256 for conditional-expectation.tex (5885f5bb...), its annex (3fddcca4...) and regular-conditional-laws.tex (02f6e868...) no longer match the files (now cb5c3355..., b0785ebd..., b337636c...); body_lines are shifted (e.g. C005 recorded 111-129, now 122-140). Exact texts remain verbatim except conditional-expectation C020 (added identically-equal clarification) and regular-conditional-laws C002 (added pointer to sec:p15-w02b-p15-008-ae-kernels). The packet reader_evidence hashes are stale the same way.

The necessity claim for the regular-conditional-probability special case rests on citation only; the source's own explanation at p. 214 (countable additivity holds only almost surely for each disjoint sequence, so exceptional sets can accumulate) is also not reproduced; line 41 (exceptional set can initially depend on A) is the nearest statement.

Conditional Cauchy-Schwarz: the proof treats D>0 and D=0 and then says all cases are supplied; D<0 is not mentioned (it is excluded at the remaining points because the quadratic is nonnegative for every real t, but this is not stated).
Norm axioms other than the triangle inequality (finite p) and all axioms for p=infinity are asserted to follow from the nonnegative integral laws or pointwise properties without displayed steps.

Spherical model: the cross-product length cos(phi), the identity r(Theta',Psi)=r(Theta,Phi) (by named elementary sine and cosine identities) and the null probability of coordinate duplications are stated without displayed computation.

The phrase attributing to the source its sphere calculation and alternative conditioning-coordinate example can be read as attributing the Y/(1+X) null-event example of thm:p15-conditioning-coordinate-examples to the source, which is not in Durrett Section 4.1 (pp. 205-217); read as the great-circle alternative coordinates of Example 4.1.8 it is supported. The theorem itself does not attribute the Y/(1+X) example.

Source variant note: Durrett's 'nice' (printed p. 53) asks only for a 1-1 map into R with measurable inverse, without a Borel image; the handbook's hypothesis requires a Borel image E and states that it makes the image and concentration requirements explicit. Recorded for the source-fidelity review; not a coverage gap for this entry.
